exposure: Impaired gestational fasting glycemia (elevated fasting glucose only)
Impaired gestational glucose tolerance (elevated 1- and/or 2-hour glucose levels)
outcome: Pregnancy complications (e.g., urinary tract infection, preeclampsia)
Neonatal outcomes (APGAR scores, birth weight, 30-minute glucose levels, probability of being discharged alive)
finding: While the formal prevalence of gestational diabetes is high in Tajikistan, this does not translate into adverse pregnancy outcomes for women with impaired gestational fasting glycemia, only those with impaired gestational glucose tolerance.
mod_finding: Women with impaired gestational glucose tolerance had more emergency cesarean sections (13.2% vs. 4.4%, p=0.002).
birth_weight: Neonates from pregnancies with impaired gestational glucose tolerance had lower birth weights (p<0.05)
